video.title: Ep 02 - “I’ve Never Seen a Model Say ‘This File Is Getting Too Big'

abstract: This Next Token episode starts as a critique of AI-industry messaging—bad rollout comms, vague AGI promises, and the gap between hype and ordinary users’ reactions—then turns into a detailed walkthrough of Dillon Mulroy’s day-to-day agentic coding workflow. The practical half is the real draw: a disciplined stack built around Pi, Herder, Plannotator, typed specs, conversation branching, and local review to keep AI-generated code understandable.
mainTakeaway: AI coding works best when it is constrained by clear tools, explicit plans, type-shaped specs, and relentless human review —not when developers hand over the keyboard and hope the agent invents good architecture on its own.

conclusion: The conversation lands in a realistic place: the hosts are genuinely excited about AI, but they trust it only inside workflows that preserve taste, accountability, and review. That combination—enthusiasm without surrender—is what makes the episode useful, and it also explains the burnout note at the end: sustaining this pace requires better habits, not just better models.
